analysis.title: Technical Advantage: Spooky price action
key_insights: BofA technical strategists see four headwinds into US midterms: rising cross-asset volatility, widening high-yield credit spreads, defensive sector rotation and declining YoY margin debt. The backdrop risks rhyming with 4Q18, with trade wars replaced by oil wars.

Risk assets such as the S&P 500 typically recover after midterms unless left-tail risks materialize. A decline to the rising trend line and 50wk SMA near 7,210 is seen as notable support if the usual correction and rebound plays out.
S&P 500: BofA reiterates hedging equity longs with 1-3m SPX 7,500 puts, particularly if long the underlying, or at minimum a more equal-weight portfolio as RSP breaks higher versus SPY.

S&P 500 daily chart is forming a head-and-shoulders top similar to Sept-Oct 2018. A decline below 7,616 breaks the neckline and favors an initial decline to 7,395 while price stays below the right-shoulder high of 7,771.

S&P 500 weekly chart has not followed through on the bullish pennant formed in August when the 7,741 year-ahead target was reached. A close below 7,504 would confirm a double top. BofA keeps a slight long bias but favors put hedges.
DXY: BofA keeps a long-USD bias with the 102.86 target reached. It expects a dip toward ~100.50, then a move toward 104.59-105, and prefers USD longs versus EUR, CHF, GBP, SEK and PHP.

EURUSD: BofA advises selling rallies in the 1.13-1.1353 area into the Fed/ECB meetings, targeting 1.10 / 1.0882 and possibly the 1.06s. The bias stays bearish while below 1.1432 / 1.1498. The euro hit a new low of 1.1113 on Oct 14 after above-survey CPI, then retraced half of its losses on the day.
EURCAD resolved its triangle lower, confirming a top with a target of 1.5479, then the 200wk SMA at 1.5278 and 1.5113. The bias is bearish while below the 50wk SMA (1.6079) / 1.6139.

US 10Y yield: the uptrend has exhausted and a corrective retracement is underway. Initial support is at 4.92-5.02%, a decline could approach ~4.81%, and 4.74% should hold. BofA advises patience before paying (betting on higher yields) again.

Copper: the bearish break below rising wedge support strengthens the case for a top. A weekly close below 13,926 confirms it and favors 13,192 / 12,913 and potentially 11,700. A breakout above 14,700 would weaken the setup.
Commodity trends diverge: oil patterns imply further upside toward the $129s, and gold's YTD correction likely needs more time or depth.

Cross-asset stress gauges are at or near key resistance. VIX needs a close above 19.45 and a higher high than 22.31. MOVE above 115 would confirm the midyear uptrend. CVIX above 7.10 signals FX carry-unwind risk. CDX HY above about 360bp opens a move toward 400bp.
Cross-sector relative strength is turning defensive: XLY/XLP and XLB/XLP broke down so Staples are outperforming, XLV/XLK is breaking higher, and XLE/XLK has Energy leading Tech since June.

YoY margin debt growth eased to +31% in Sept from +37% in Aug and May's +54% peak. Total debt is ~$1.48tn, below June's record. The 54% peak is the fourth highest since 1998, and the three higher peaks preceded equity declines.
Seasonality: in Year 2 of the presidential cycle, SPX historically rises in Oct and Nov, with up ratios around 67%. In 2018, SPX instead sold off sharply in Q4 and ended the year down more than 6.5%.
After a September record high, SPX rose in 22 of 25 Q4s, 88% of the time, by +3.72% on average versus +2.89% for all Q4s. Left-tail outcomes were -28.88% in 1929 and -13.97% in 2018.

sector_views.rationale: XLY/XLP broke below its 2022 uptrend line and XLB/XLP broke below its 50wk SMA, so Staples are beginning to outperform Discretionary and Materials.
XLE/XLK has Energy leading Technology since June after a deep retracement, and could form a double bottom.
XLV/XLK is breaking above resistance, and follow-through would reinforce risk-off rotation while October's higher low holds.
Technology is lagging Energy and Health Care on relative strength ratios, part of the early defensive rotation away from high-beta leadership.
XLB/XLP broke below its 50wk SMA and 2025 uptrend line.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Oct 14 above-survey CPI print lifted the USD and sent EURUSD to a new low of 1.1113 before a partial rebound.
It eased from +37% in Aug and May's +54% peak, and BofA reads the turn down from an extreme as a late-cycle warning.
BofA sees the retracement as corrective and favors paying for yields to resume rising after signs of exhaustion.

tension_points.theme: SPX Q4 seasonality vs left tail
tension_points.bull_case: After a September record high, SPX rose in 22 of 25 Q4s (88%), averaging +3.72%, and midterm-year corrections are often followed by a yearend rebound.
tension_points.bear_case: Head-and-shoulders top, possible double top, falling margin debt, defensive rotation, and rising volatility and credit spreads echo 4Q18, when SPX fell 13.97% in Q4.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A close below 7,504 confirms the weekly double top and a break below 7,616 confirms the daily head and shoulders, while a move above the right-shoulder high of 7,771 would weaken the bearish setup.
